# Fix: `arms_plan=67 arms_tree=68` — section-mapping gate drift

**Gate:** `docs/audits/cf198-section-mapping.sh`
**Consumers:** `tests/selftest.sh` section 39, `docs/ACCEPTANCE-PLAN.md`
**Base:** `a8112ae` (gate reports `arms_plan=67 arms_tree=67 RESULT: OK`)
**Working tree:** gate reports `arms_plan=67 arms_tree=68 RESULT: FAIL`

## 1. Root-cause analysis

The gate is a **derived-count / cross-artifact consistency check**:

| Quantity | Derived from | Working tree |
|---|---|---|
| `arms_tree` | `^say "N\.` numbered section markers in `tests/selftest.sh` | **68** |
| `arms_plan` | `| §N |` mapping rows in `docs/ACCEPTANCE-PLAN.md` | **67** |

The diff under test adds a new numbered selftest section (arm **§65**) but does **not** add its `| §65 |` row to the plan. The artifacts are out of sync by one row. The fix is to make the plan describe the new arm — never to weaken the gate.

**Trap 1 — "pre-existing" is wrong.** There *is* a genuinely pre-existing failure nearby (section 56, unrelated port/auth battery). The discriminator is to rebuild the audit at base in a detached worktree: base `a8112ae` → `67/67 OK`; working tree → `67/68 FAIL`. Green-at-base / red-in-tree means the diff introduced it.

**Trap 2 — over-broad hermeticity arm.** The audit's "tracked files untouched" arm must be scoped to the paths the fixtures write, not `git status` of the whole tree, or it fails on the very diff being gated.

## 2. Exact fix

**2a. Derive the missing id** (don't hard-code blindly):

```bash
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
comm -23 \
  <(grep -oE '^say "[0-9]+\.' tests/selftest.sh | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | LC_ALL=C sort -u) \
  <(grep -oE '^\| *§[0-9]+ *\|' docs/ACCEPTANCE-PLAN.md | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | LC_ALL=C sort -u)
# expected: 65
grep -nE '^say "65\.' tests/selftest.sh   # title source for the new row
```

**2b. Add the `§65` row** to `docs/ACCEPTANCE-PLAN.md`, matching neighbouring `§64`/`§66` columns:

```markdown
| §65 | <title from tests/selftest.sh> | <status, matching neighbours> |
```

**2c. Bump the prose arm count 67 → 68** in `docs/ACCEPTANCE-PLAN.md`:

```bash
grep -nE '\b(67|sixty-seven)\b' docs/ACCEPTANCE-PLAN.md
```

**2d. Scope the hermeticity arm** in `docs/audits/cf198-section-mapping.sh`. Replace whole-tree `git status` with a fixture-path snapshot:

```bash
FIXTURE_PATHS=(  # the exact paths the audit fixtures write
  # "docs/ACCEPTANCE-PLAN.md.fixture"  ...
)
snapshot() { git status --porcelain -- "${FIXTURE_PATHS[@]}"; }
before="$(snapshot)"
# ... run fixtures ...
after="$(snapshot)"
if [ "$before" != "$after" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: fixtures touched tracked files:" >&2; printf '%s\n' "$after" >&2; exit 1
fi
```

## 3. Verification

```bash
# 3.1 reproduce
bash docs/audits/cf198-section-mapping.sh        # 67/68 FAIL

# 3.2 prove introduced by the diff (Trap 1)
BASE=a8112ae
WT="$(mktemp -d /tmp/cf198-base.XXXXXX)"
git worktree add --detach "$WT" "$BASE"
( cd "$WT" && bash docs/audits/cf198-section-mapping.sh )   # 67/67 OK
( cd "$WT" && bash tests/selftest.sh 56 || true )           # still fails -> pre-existing
git worktree remove --force "$WT"; git worktree prune

# 3.3 after fix
bash docs/audits/cf198-section-mapping.sh        # 68/68 OK
bash tests/selftest.sh 39                        # PASS

# 3.5 scoped arm still catches real leakage
printf '\n' >> <one-fixture-path>
bash docs/audits/cf198-section-mapping.sh        # FAIL
git checkout -- <one-fixture-path>
bash docs/audits/cf198-section-mapping.sh        # OK
```

| Check | Expected |
|---|---|
| `arms_plan == arms_tree` | `68 == 68` |
| Gate result | `RESULT: OK`, exit 0 |
| selftest section 39 | PASS |
| Base `a8112ae` | `67/67 OK` |
| Section 56 | still fails — pre-existing, out of scope |

## Appendix — mechanic verification

The real repo was absent, so I exercised the mechanics on a minimal synthetic mirror (67 arms/rows, count check, whole-tree hermeticity). Observed:

```text
base run                                 67/67 RESULT: OK
add new tree arm                         67/68 RESULT: FAIL
comm -23 tree_ids plan_ids               68
add plan row (counts match)              68/68 RESULT: FAIL  (whole-tree status sees both modified files)
scope hermeticity to FIXTURE_PATHS       68/68 RESULT: OK
git worktree add --detach <base>; run    67/67 RESULT: OK
```

This confirms the count-drift diagnosis, the `comm` missing-id derivation, the base-vs-tree worktree discriminator (Trap 1), and fixture-path scoping (Trap 2). In the real repo the derived missing id is `65` instead of the synthetic `68`.

---
Saved at `/workspace/SOLUTION.md`.

signatures.description: A test gate that derives an expected count from one artifact and compares it to another (here: docs/audits/cf198-section-mapping.sh counts `^say "N\.` markers in tests/selftest.sh and requires one `| §N |` row per arm in docs/ACCEPTANCE-PLAN.md, wired as selftest section 39) fails as `arms_plan=67 arms_tree=68` whenever a new numbered section is added without its plan row. Two traps follow. (1) The gate failure is caused by the very diff under test, but an agent that only reads the message calls it 'pre-existing', exactly like the genuinely pre-existing failure sitting next to it (section 56, an unrelated port/auth battery) — the discriminator is to rebuild the audit in a detached worktree at the base commit (`git worktree add --detach <tmp> <base>`) and run it there: base gives 67/67 OK, the working tree gives 67/68. (2) The gate's own 'tracked files untouched' arm must scope to the files the fixtures mutate, not to `git status` of the whole tree, or it fails on the diff that is being gated.
